title: Aging artists: Rudolph, Lee Whipper and Eubie Blake
summary: Johnston and Gil talk about very old performers who are still active.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh, incredible. I was going to say another thing is that ten years ago

we were much less enlightened about geriatrics than we are now. And I would certainly say that since most of my work involves theater people and musicians who are anywhere from 75 which eliminates you, but from 75 to 96 years old I have come to know a great deal, to learn a great deal, about older people.
I was telling you about Rudolph (Bremwald?). Did you hear about him? He's fantastic. I saw a picture of him in that High Fidelity magazine. He's ninety years old?
Very spry. A full head of black hair, right?

That's fantastic. And Lee Whipper (Dr. Ripley) is 96. And the only thing that slows him down, I've just talked to him today, the actor, and the only thing that slows him down is his eyesight and that doesn't slow him down too much. But I've really learned a great deal about them.
